title: Chengjiang Fossil Site
summary: Early Cambrian fossil site in Yunnan, China, preserving soft-bodied animals in fine detail. At least 16 phyla and about 196 species are documented, including some of the earliest known chordates and vertebrates, making it a key record of the rapid diversification of animal life.

uncertainty.note: IUGS gives approximately 518 Ma (Cambrian Epoch 2, Age 3); UNESCO gives 530 million years before present. The range spans both.

as_recorded.value: Cambrian Epoch 2, Age 3 (Approximately 518 million years ago)

when.display: about 518 million years ago (early Cambrian; UNESCO says 530)

where.modern_name: Chengjiang County (Maotianshan area), Yuxi, Yunnan Province, China
where.historical_name: Shallow marine basin on the South China block; no polities exist at this date

paleo.plate_model: MERDITH2021 (Merdith et al. 2021, Earth-Science Reviews 214:103477) via GPlates Web Service
paleo.note: Point 24.67 N, 102.98 E reconstructed to 518 Ma. Model frames differ in absolute position, so the value is indicative.

importance.justification: One of the two best-known Cambrian soft-bodied fossil sites, with the earliest known vertebrates.

reviewer_note: Two opened sources disagree on age: UNESCO 530 Ma and IUGS about 518 Ma; the record uses 518 with a 12 Ma range. Coordinates are UNESCO's property point, 24 40 8 N, 102 58 38 E, matching IUGS. Merdith 2021 paleo-position is indicative only.
